newsitem.title: USA: Maine ends fiscal year with $60 million surplus.
newsitem.headline: Maine ends fiscal year with $60 million surplus.

text.p: Maine closed out the 1997 fiscal year with a $60 million surplus in general fund revenues and $175 million cash on hand, Gov. Angus King's office said Thursday.
"What this means is that for the first time in seven years the state will not have to borrow money in anticipation of tax revenues in order to pay its bills," King said in a prepared statement.

Nearly $45 million will be used for tax relief although the exact method to do that has not been established. A program to decrease the unfunded liability of the state pension system will receive $14.9 million.
King called financial situation the "best revenue picture in 10 years," and credited it to Maine's improved economy and good fiscal management by his office and the lawmakers.
